answer: Randomness-gated proof slots. Each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws a per-agent slot from a global nadir threshold; agents must submit a proof within their slot to stay active. An attacker precomputing identities cannot predict slot assignment, so mass registration yields many dormant agents. Each fake identity costs a full slot-window of monitoring and a quill-signed proof per epoch. Slots are recycled only on validated lotus-style chained draws, forcing sustained per-identity compute.
